```{r setup, include=FALSE}
#Define custom functions
#AMOVA permutation test (amova.fn / randamova.fn from my_functions): draws the null histogram, optionally saves it to
#'file', and returns the observed statistic and p-value (amovapval.fn only plots). p = proportion of permutations >= observed.
#Note: amova.fn's statistic has a ~0.5 baseline, so only the p-value is interpretable.
amova_test=function(distmat,cell_key,iterations=30000,plottitle="",file=NULL,seed=20261031){
  groupnames=unique(cell_key$Cell_type)
  set.seed(seed)
  obs=amova.fn(distmat=distmat,groupnames=groupnames,cell_key=cell_key)
  rnd=sapply(1:iterations,function(i) randamova.fn(distmat=distmat,groupnames=groupnames,cell_key=cell_key))
  p=mean(rnd>=obs)
  draw=function(){
    hist(rnd,col="grey",100,main=plottitle,xlab="AMOVA statistic",xlim=range(c(rnd,obs)))
    abline(v=obs,col="red",lwd=2)
    legend("topright",legend=paste0("Observed\n p = ",signif(p,digits=2)),lwd=2,col="red",bty="n")
  }
  draw()
  if(!is.null(file)) {pdf(file,width=5,height=4); draw(); dev.off()}
  data.frame(n_colonies=nrow(distmat),statistic=obs,null_mean=mean(rnd),p_value=p,iterations=iterations)
}
plot_96profile=function(df,colnames=c("sampleID","chr","pos","ref","alt"),genomeFile,title=NULL) {
  require(Rsamtools)
  require(GenomicRanges)
  require(IRanges)
  mutations = data.frame(sampleID=df[[colnames[1]]],
                         chr=df[[colnames[2]]],
                         pos=df[[colnames[3]]],
                         ref=df[[colnames[4]]],
                         trinuc_ref= "-",
                         mut=df[[colnames[5]]])
  mutations_GRange<-GRanges(mutations$chr, IRanges::IRanges(mutations$pos-1, mutations$pos+1))
  mutations$trinuc_ref = as.vector(Rsamtools::scanFa(file=genomeFile,mutations_GRange ))
  
  ntcomp = c(T="A",G="C",C="G",A="T")
  mutations$sub = paste(mutations$ref,mutations$mut,sep=">")
  mutations$trinuc_ref_py = mutations$trinuc_ref
  for (j in 1:nrow(mutations)) {
    if (mutations$ref[j] %in% c("A","G")) { # Purine base
      mutations$sub[j] = paste(ntcomp[mutations$ref[j]],ntcomp[mutations$mut[j]],sep=">")
      mutations$trinuc_ref_py[j] = paste(ntcomp[rev(strsplit(mutations$trinuc_ref[j],split="")[[1]])],collapse="")
    }
  }
  freqs = table(paste(mutations$sub,paste(substr(mutations$trinuc_ref_py,1,1),substr(mutations$trinuc_ref_py,3,3),sep="-"),sep=","))
  sub_vec = c("C>A","C>G","C>T","T>A","T>C","T>G")
  ctx_vec = paste(rep(c("A","C","G","T"),each=4),rep(c("A","C","G","T"),times=4),sep="-")
  full_vec = paste(rep(sub_vec,each=16),rep(ctx_vec,times=6),sep=",")
  freqs_full = freqs[full_vec]; freqs_full[is.na(freqs_full)] = 0; names(freqs_full) = full_vec
  
  xstr = paste(substr(full_vec,5,5), substr(full_vec,1,1), substr(full_vec,7,7), sep="")
  
  #pdf("Mut_Sig_fetal_shared.pdf")
  colvec = rep(c("dodgerblue","black","red","grey70","olivedrab3","plum2"),each=16)
  y = freqs_full; maxy = max(y)
  h = barplot(y, las=2, col=colvec, border=NA, ylim=c(0,maxy*1.5), space=1, cex.names=0.6, names.arg=xstr, ylab="Number mutations",main=title)
  for (j in 1:length(sub_vec)) {
    xpos = h[c((j-1)*16+1,j*16)]
    rect(xpos[1]-0.5, maxy*1.2, xpos[2]+0.5, maxy*1.3, border=NA, col=colvec[j*16])
    text(x=mean(xpos), y=maxy*1.3, pos=3, label=sub_vec[j])
  }
}

plot_96profile_mutref=function(mutref_vec,genomeFile,title=NULL) {
  mut_mat=stringr::str_split(mutref_vec,pattern="-",simplify=T)
  colnames(mut_mat)=c("chr","pos","ref","alt")
  df=as.data.frame(mut_mat)%>%
    mutate(pos=as.integer(pos))%>%
    mutate(sampleID="this_sample",.before=1)
  plot_96profile(df,genomeFile = genomeFile,title=title)
}

vaf_density_plot_final=function(sample,tree,COMB_mats,private_only=F){
  node <- which(tree$tip.label==sample)
  if(private_only) {relevant_nodes<-node} else {relevant_nodes<-get_ancestral_nodes(node,tree$edge)}
  sample_muts <- COMB_mats$mat$mut_ref[COMB_mats$mat$node %in% relevant_nodes]
  COMB_mats$NR[COMB_mats$NR == 0] <- 1
  dens <- density((COMB_mats$NV/COMB_mats$NR)[sample_muts,sample])
  plot(dens,xlim = c(0,1),main=sample)
  abline(v = dens$x[which.max(dens$y)])
  text(0.7, max(dens$y) - 0.2, paste("Peak VAF dens=",round(dens$x[which.max(dens$y)], digits = 2)),col="red",cex = 0.7)
}
```

## Plot trees with tissue source info

In this plot, branches are coloured by the specific tissue colour if all the descendants are from the same tissue.
If descendants come from different tissues, the colour is black.

```{r plot_source,fig.width=12, fig.height=5}

#Can choose the 
plot_sharing_multiple=function(tree,details,matrices,node,cat_df,cat_name="cat",sharing_cols=c("dark green","red","orange","brown","green"),...){  
  library(dplyr)
  categories=cat_df%>%filter(sample%in%tree$tip.label)%>%pull(cat_name)%>%unique()
  if(length(categories)>length(sharing_cols)) {stop("Not enough colours supplied for number of categories")}
  info=get_edge_info(tree,details,node=node)
  sample_categories=cat_df%>%filter(sample%in%info$samples)%>%pull(cat_name)
  if(length(unique(sample_categories))>1) {
    sharing_info <- "shared"
  } else {
    sharing_info <- unique(sample_categories)
  }
  sharing_cols=sharing_cols[1:length(categories)]
  
  #Add black as the first "shared" category colour
  if(all(categories%in%names(sharing_cols))) {
    sharing_cols<-sharing_cols[categories]
    sharing_cols<-c("black",sharing_cols)
    names(sharing_cols)[1]="shared"
  } else {
    sharing_cols<-c("black",sharing_cols)
    names(sharing_cols)=c("shared",categories)
  }
  
  if(length(tree$edge.length[tree$edge[,2]==node])>0){
    arrows(y0=info$yb,y1=info$yt,x0=info$x,x1=info$x,length=0,col=sharing_cols[sharing_info],lend=1,...)
  }
}
```

## AMOVA (Analysis of molecular variance)

This is a statistical measure of whether samples are more clustered by cell source than you would expect by chance.
This is done on the ultrametric tree.

```{r AMOVA}
cellkey<-sample_level_metadata%>%
  dplyr::mutate("Sample"=INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME)%>%
  dplyr::filter(Sample%in%tree$tip.label)%>%
  dplyr::select(Sample,TISSUE_PHENOTYPE)%>%
  dplyr::rename("Cell_type"=TISSUE_PHENOTYPE)

distmat <- cophenetic(drop.tip(tree.ultra,"Ancestral"))

amova_res<-amova_test(distmat = distmat,
                      cell_key = cellkey,
                      iterations = 30000,
                      plottitle = paste0(sample_ID,": Phylogenetic clustering by cell source"),
                      file = if(resave_plots) paste0(plots_dir,sample_ID,"_AMOVA_uncorrected_tree.pdf") else NULL)
amova_res

```

## Plot the mutational signatures

Shared mutations are highly confident to be acquired in vivo as they are present in two independent sorted colonies. 
Private mutations may - in theory - be a combination of in vivo acquired and in vitro acquired mutations. 
Looking at the mutational signatures of the two may give a clue as to any differences.

Differences may be due to:

(1) in vitro-acquired mutations that have a different mutational signature \
(2) differences in in vivo mutational process between mutations acquired early in embryogenesis (these are more likely to be shared) and those acquired later (these are likely to be private)

For reasons explained later, the differences are likely due to in vitro-acquired mutations in this case. The chunk below needs the reference genome (`gfile`), so it is not run. See 'Mutational signatures of clonal and sub-clonal private mutations' below for the comparison using the clonal/sub-clonal assignment.

```{r mutational_signatures, eval=FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(2,1))
plot_96profile(df = details%>%mutate(sampleID=sample_ID)%>%filter(node%in%1:length(tree$tip.label)),colnames = c("sampleID","Chrom","Pos","Ref","Alt"),genomeFile = gfile,title="Private mutations")
plot_96profile(df = details%>%mutate(sampleID=sample_ID)%>%filter(!node%in%1:length(tree$tip.label)),colnames = c("sampleID","Chrom","Pos","Ref","Alt"),genomeFile = gfile, title="Shared mutations")

```

## Look at the VAF density plots of the private mutations in a few individual samples

Here, we choose the first 16 tips of the tree and looks at the VAF density plots of the private mutations. If all the private mutations were clonal these would all have neat peaks at 0.5.  However, clearly there are significant numbers of sub-clonal mutations that are likely to be in vitro. Note that every private mutation on the tree has NV >= 3 and VAF >= 0.2 (tree-building filter), so the lower part of the sub-clonal peak is cut off, more so at low depth.

```{r VAF_plots, echo=FALSE,fig.height=12,fig.width=12}

```

## Review the VAF histograms of all private mutations from all samples

What is the overall story here?  What proportion of private mutations are in fact subclonal or artefactual?

```{r VAF_plots_private}
COMB_mats=filtered_muts$COMB_mats.tree.build

#Concatentate all variant read counts (of private mutations) into single vector
all_NV<-lapply(head(tree$tip.label,-1),function(sample) {
  node <- which(tree$tip.label==sample)
  sample_muts <- COMB_mats$mat$mut_ref[COMB_mats$mat$node %in% node]
  COMB_mats$NR[COMB_mats$NR == 0] <- 1
  return(COMB_mats$NV[sample_muts,sample])
})%>%unlist()

#Concatentate all depth counts into single vector
all_NR<-lapply(head(tree$tip.label,-1),function(Sample) {
  node <- which(tree$tip.label==Sample)
  sample_muts <- COMB_mats$mat$mut_ref[COMB_mats$mat$node %in% node]
  COMB_mats$NR[COMB_mats$NR == 0] <- 1
  sample_NR=COMB_mats$NR[sample_muts,Sample]
  names(sample_NR)<-sample_muts
  return(sample_NR)
})%>%unlist()

#Plot as a density map
dens <- density(all_NV[all_NR>20]/all_NR[all_NR>20])
plot(dens,xlim = c(0,1),main=paste0(sample_ID,": all high depth private mutations"))
abline(v = dens$x[which.max(dens$y)])
text(0.7, max(dens$y) - 0.2, paste("Peak VAF dens=",round(dens$x[which.max(dens$y)], digits = 2)),col="red",cex = 0.7)

```


### Separate clonal and sub-clonal private mutations (detection-aware mixture)

The VAF plots above show that many private mutations are sub-clonal: they were acquired in the colony after the founder cell (VAF ~0.25) rather than being clonal (VAF ~0.5). Not every clonal mutation is detected either. The previous version of this section fitted a binomial mixture to mutations with depth > 20, then made Bayesian hard calls per mutation and per sample. It is archived in `archive/Mouse_phylo_initial_before_burden_correction.Rmd`. That approach was biased because detection depends on depth:

- A private mutation is only on the tree if NV >= 3 and VAF >= 0.2 (tree-building filter). Sub-clonal mutations are therefore lost far more often at low depth, so the depth > 20 mutations (a minority; median colony depth ~17-19x) over-represent them.
- The apparent "0.33" sub-clonal peak is a ~0.26 component truncated at VAF 0.2.
- Male X/Y mutations are hemizygous (VAF ~1 at half depth) and were treated as diploid.

The correction now used (`burden_correction/`; see its README for the method and a simulation test with known truth) accounts for how mutations reach the tree:

1. The clonal/sub-clonal mixture is fitted *conditional on detection*: beta-binomial clonal and sub-clonal components shared across colonies, a clonal weight per colony, and partial detection of calls with exactly 3 variant reads. X/Y mutations are modelled with twice the VAF.
2. Clonal sensitivity = the pipeline's germline-SNP sensitivity (recovered from the input tree: tip SNV count / tip edge length) x the probability that a clonal mutation passes the VAF filter at that colony's depth.
3. Corrected private branch = expected number of detected clonal SNVs / clonal sensitivity. Shared branches are rebuilt from raw SNV counts and divided by the probability that at least one descendant colony detects a mutation.

In simulations this is within +-2% of the true clonal burden. The previous hard-call correction underestimated it by 8-27%, depending on depth. The correction uses SNVs only, because the trees were built from SNVs. The fit is saved in `burden_correction/results/` and reloaded if present.

Each private SNV also gets a posterior probability of being clonal, P(clonal), from the fitted mixture and its colony's clonal weight. Detection terms cancel for a single detected mutation, so this probability is valid at any depth. Hard calls are uncertain at low depth, though. For that reason the burden correction sums the probabilities rather than counting hard calls.

```{r burden_correction}
bc_file=paste0(my_working_dir,"burden_correction/results/burden_correction_",sample_ID,".Rds")
if(file.exists(bc_file)) {
  bc=readRDS(bc_file)
} else {
  bc=correct_branch_lengths(tree=read.tree(paste0(my_working_dir,"tree_files/tree_",sample_ID,"_postMS_reduced_a_j_vaf_post_mix_post_dup.tree")),
                            COMB_mats=filtered_muts$COMB_mats.tree.build,sex="male")
}

#Fitted global parameters
data.frame(clonal_VAF=unname(bc$fit$pc),subclonal_VAF=unname(bc$fit$ps),rho_clonal=bc$fit$rho[1],rho_subclonal=bc$fit$rho[2],
           detection_NV3=bc$fit$delta[1],detection_NV4=bc$fit$delta[2])%>%signif(3)

#Per-mutation assignments
priv<-bc$priv%>%
  mutate(vaf_adj=NV/NR/cf, #X/Y VAFs halved so that they are on the diploid scale
         assignment=ifelse(p_clonal>0.5,"clonal","sub-clonal"),
         confidence=case_when(p_clonal>0.9~"clonal (P>0.9)",p_clonal<0.1~"sub-clonal (P<0.1)",TRUE~"uncertain"))

data.frame(private_SNVs=nrow(priv),
           expected_clonal=round(sum(priv$p_clonal)),
           expected_subclonal=round(sum(1-priv$p_clonal)),
           MAP_clonal=sum(priv$assignment=="clonal"),
           MAP_subclonal=sum(priv$assignment=="sub-clonal"),
           confident_clonal=sum(priv$p_clonal>0.9),
           confident_subclonal=sum(priv$p_clonal<0.1))

#VAF distribution of private SNVs, coloured by assignment confidence
vaf_by_depth_plot<-priv%>%
  mutate(depth=cut(NR,c(0,10,15,20,30,Inf),labels=c("<=10x","11-15x","16-20x","21-30x",">30x")))%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=vaf_adj,fill=factor(confidence,levels=c("sub-clonal (P<0.1)","uncertain","clonal (P>0.9)"))))+
  geom_histogram(binwidth=0.025,boundary=0)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=c(bc$fit$ps,bc$fit$pc),linetype=2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=bc$fit$min_vaf,col="red",linetype=3)+
  facet_wrap(~depth,scales="free_y",nrow=1)+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#D55E00","grey70","#0072B2"))+
  theme_classic()+theme(legend.position="bottom")+
  labs(x="VAF (X/Y halved)",y="Private SNVs",fill=NULL,
       title=paste0(sample_ID,": private SNVs by depth (dashed: fitted VAFs; red: VAF filter)"))
vaf_by_depth_plot
save_gg(vaf_by_depth_plot,paste0(sample_ID,"_private_VAF_by_depth"),width=11,height=3.5)

#Distribution of P(clonal)
p_clonal_plot<-priv%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=p_clonal))+
  geom_histogram(binwidth=0.025,boundary=0,fill="grey50")+
  theme_classic()+
  labs(x="P(clonal)",y="Private SNVs",title=paste0(sample_ID,": posterior probability of being clonal"))
p_clonal_plot
save_gg(p_clonal_plot,paste0(sample_ID,"_private_P_clonal"),width=4,height=3)

#Per-colony clonal weight against depth
bc$samples%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=median_depth,y=w_clonal))+
  geom_point(size=1)+
  theme_classic()+
  labs(x="Median depth at private sites",y="Clonal weight (true-space fraction)",title=paste0(sample_ID,": clonal fraction of private SNVs per colony"))
```

### Mutational signatures of clonal and sub-clonal private mutations

If sub-clonal private mutations are acquired in culture, their signature should differ from in vivo mutations. Shared mutations are the in vivo reference. Contexts come from the cache made by `burden_correction/signatures_by_clonality.R`. That script fetches them from the GRCm38 reference on the farm and also does the fits and bootstraps for both mice together.

Each set is shown three ways:
- **weighted:** every mutation counts in proportion to P(clonal) or 1 - P(clonal);
- **most likely assignment (MAP);**
- **high confidence:** P > 0.9 or P < 0.1.

```{r signatures_by_clonality,fig.height=12,fig.width=12}
ctx_file=paste0(my_working_dir,"burden_correction/results/signatures/contexts.Rds")
if(!file.exists(ctx_file)) stop("Run burden_correction/signatures_by_clonality.R first to fetch the trinucleotide contexts")
ctx=readRDS(ctx_file)

#96-channel classification (pyrimidine reference, MutationalPatterns order)
comp=c(A="T",C="G",G="C",T="A")
rc=function(x) sapply(strsplit(x,""),function(b) paste(rev(comp[b]),collapse=""))
classify=function(mut_ref,tri){p=do.call(rbind,strsplit(mut_ref,"-")); ref=p[,3]; alt=p[,4]
  flip=ref%in%c("G","A"); tri2=ifelse(flip,rc(tri),tri); ref2=ifelse(flip,comp[ref],ref); alt2=ifelse(flip,comp[alt],alt)
  paste0(substr(tri2,1,1),"[",ref2,">",alt2,"]",substr(tri2,3,3))}
channels=MutationalPatterns:::TRIPLETS_96
ctx$channel=classify(ctx$mut_ref,ctx$tri)

shared_snvs=details%>%filter(Mut_type=="SNV" & !node%in%1:length(tree$tip.label))%>%pull(mut_ref)
sets=bind_rows(data.frame(mut_ref=shared_snvs,set="shared",w=1),
               priv%>%transmute(mut_ref,set="clonal (weighted)",w=p_clonal),
               priv%>%transmute(mut_ref,set="sub-clonal (weighted)",w=1-p_clonal),
               priv%>%filter(p_clonal>0.5)%>%transmute(mut_ref,set="clonal (MAP)",w=1),
               priv%>%filter(p_clonal<=0.5)%>%transmute(mut_ref,set="sub-clonal (MAP)",w=1),
               priv%>%filter(p_clonal>0.9)%>%transmute(mut_ref,set="clonal (P>0.9)",w=1),
               priv%>%filter(p_clonal<0.1)%>%transmute(mut_ref,set="sub-clonal (P<0.1)",w=1))%>%
  left_join(ctx%>%dplyr::select(mut_ref,channel),by="mut_ref")
if(any(is.na(sets$channel))) stop("Contexts missing for some mutations: rerun burden_correction/signatures_by_clonality.R")
set_levels=unique(sets$set)
M=sapply(set_levels,function(s) {x=sets%>%filter(set==s); tapply(x$w,factor(x$channel,levels=channels),sum,default=0)})

#Restricted fit to signatures seen in HSCs and in culture, C>T at CpG (SBS1 hallmark) and similarity to shared mutations
sigs=get_known_signatures(muttype="snv",source="COSMIC",genome="mm10"); rownames(sigs)=channels
fit=fit_to_signatures(M,sigs[,c("SBS1","SBS5","SBS18")])$contribution
cpg=grepl("\\[C>T\\]G",channels)
data.frame(set=set_levels,n=round(colSums(M)),
           CpG_CtoT=round(colSums(M[cpg,])/colSums(M),3),
           round(t(fit)/colSums(fit),3),
           cos_to_shared=round(apply(M,2,function(x) cos_sim(x,M[,"shared"])),3),row.names=NULL)

signature_plot<-plot_96_profile(M[,c("shared","clonal (P>0.9)","clonal (weighted)","sub-clonal (weighted)","sub-clonal (P<0.1)")],ymax=0.1,condensed=TRUE)
signature_plot
save_gg(signature_plot,paste0(sample_ID,"_signatures_by_clonality"),width=12,height=10)
```

Clonal private mutations have almost the same profile as shared mutations: SBS1-rich, with peaks of C>T at CpG. Sub-clonal ones are depleted of SBS1 and dominated by non-CpG C>T spread across contexts. The separation grows with assignment confidence, which supports the mixture classification. This fits sub-clonal mutations being acquired in culture, although low-VAF artefacts would look similar. Both mice show the same pattern; see `burden_correction/README.md` for the combined fits and bootstrap intervals.

### Using these corrected mutation burdens

The corrected private branch is the expected number of clonal SNVs, P(clonal) summed over the colony's private SNVs, divided by the colony's clonal sensitivity. Shared branches are corrected for sensitivity only. Corrected total burdens are 91.9 for MD7634 (standard error of the mean 1.5) and 79.8 for MD7635 (SEM 2.0); corrected private burdens are 61.9 and 53.3. These replace the earlier estimates, which are not comparable: uniform correction 69.9 / 66.6, sample-specific correction 76.5 / 70.4. The mice differ mainly through caller sensitivity (median 0.84 vs 0.92) and the sub-clonal fraction. Burdens differ little between tissues (MD7634: iliac slightly lower, Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.011 for private burden; MD7635: p = 0.2).

```{r private_branch_correction}
#Per-sample: observed private SNVs, clonal weight, sensitivity and corrected burdens
mut_burden_df<-bc$samples%>%
  left_join(sample_level_metadata,by=c("sample"="INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME"))%>%
  dplyr::rename(sampleID=sample,mut_burden=total_burden)
mut_burden_df%>%dplyr::select(sampleID,TISSUE_PHENOTYPE,n_obs,w_clonal,caller_sensitivity,sensitivity,N_clonal,shared_burden,mut_burden)%>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric),~round(.x,2)))%>%head()

#Plot the tree with the corrected burdens
tree.corrected<-bc$tree
tree.corrected=plot_tree(tree = tree.corrected,cex.label=0,title = sample_ID)
temp=sapply(tree.corrected$tip.label,function(sample_ID) plot_category_tip_point(sample_ID = sample_ID,
                                                                  tree=tree.corrected,
                                                                  cat_df=sample_level_metadata%>%mutate("sample"=INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME),
                                                                  cols = cell_type_colours,
                                                                  cat_name="TISSUE_PHENOTYPE"))

#Plot the legend
legend("topleft", inset=c(.01,.01), title="Sample type",
       names(cell_type_colours), fill=cell_type_colours, horiz=F, cex=0.7)

## From this, look at the mutation burdens
#Overall mean mutation burden
print(paste("Mean burden is",round(mean(mut_burden_df$mut_burden),1)))
print(paste("The standard error of the mean is:",round(sd(mut_burden_df$mut_burden)/sqrt(nrow(mut_burden_df)),2)))

#Summarise mean burdens per tissue of origin
mut_burden_df%>%
  group_by(TISSUE_PHENOTYPE)%>%
  summarise(n_samples=n(),mean_private_observed=mean(n_obs),mean_private_corrected=mean(N_clonal),
            mean_burden=mean(mut_burden),median_burden=median(mut_burden))%>%
  print()
kruskal.test(N_clonal~TISSUE_PHENOTYPE,data=mut_burden_df)

#Observed vs corrected private burdens
mut_burden_df%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=n_obs,y=N_clonal,col=TISSUE_PHENOTYPE))+
  geom_point(size=1)+
  geom_abline(linetype=2)+
  scale_color_manual(values=cell_type_colours)+
  theme_classic()+
  labs(col="Tissue",x="Observed private SNVs",y="Corrected clonal private burden",title = sample_ID)

#Corrected private burden should not depend on depth
mut_burden_df%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=median_depth,y=N_clonal,col=TISSUE_PHENOTYPE))+
  geom_point(size=1)+
  scale_color_manual(values=cell_type_colours)+
  theme_classic()+
  labs(col="Tissue",x="Median depth at private sites",y="Corrected clonal private burden",
       title=paste0(sample_ID,": Spearman rho = ",round(cor(mut_burden_df$median_depth,mut_burden_df$N_clonal,method="spearman"),2)))

#Plot a histogram of the burdens, separated by tissue type
mut_burden_df%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=mut_burden,fill=TISSUE_PHENOTYPE))+
  geom_histogram(col="black",linewidth=0.2)+
  scale_fill_manual(values=cell_type_colours)+
  theme_classic()+
  coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,200))+

```

### Make a new ultrametric tree with the corrected mutation burdens

This uses the 'make.ultrametric.tree' function which is an iteratively reweighted means algorithm to scale the total sample heights all to a height of 1. We then rescale them to the mean mutation burden across samples. This gives an ultrametric tree that is still scaled to 'molecular time' (i.e. number of mutations). \

You can then look for phylogenetic clustering by tissue using AMOVA.

```{r corrected_ultrametric_tree}
tree.corrected.ultra=make.ultrametric.tree(tree.corrected)
tree.corrected.ultra$coords<-NULL
tree.corrected.ultra$edge.length[is.infinite(tree.corrected.ultra$edge.length)]<-0
tree.corrected.ultra$edge.length<-tree.corrected.ultra$edge.length*mean(get_mut_burden(tree.corrected))
tree.corrected.ultra=plot_tree(tree.corrected.ultra,cex.label=0,plot_axis = T,title = sample_ID)

#Apply the 'plot_sharing_multiple' function to colour the branches
temp=add_annotation(tree=tree.corrected.ultra,
               annot_function=plot_sharing_multiple,
               cat_df=sample_level_metadata%>%mutate("sample"=INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME),
               cat_name="TISSUE_PHENOTYPE",
               lwd=2,
               sharing_cols=cell_type_colours)

#Apply the 'plot_category_tip_point' function to create coloured tips according to the tissue
temp=sapply(tree.corrected.ultra$tip.label,function(sample_ID) plot_category_tip_point(sample_ID = sample_ID,
                                                                  tree=tree.corrected.ultra, cat_df=sample_level_metadata%>%mutate("sample"=INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME),
                                                                  cat_name="TISSUE_PHENOTYPE",
                                                                  cols=cell_type_colours,
                                                                  cex=1))

#Plot the legend
legend("topleft", inset=c(.01,.01), title="Sample type",
       names(cell_type_colours), fill=cell_type_colours, horiz=F, cex=0.7)

#Repeat the AMOVA with this version of the tree, though
cellkey<-sample_level_metadata%>%
  dplyr::mutate("Sample"=INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME)%>%
  dplyr::filter(Sample%in%tree.corrected.ultra$tip.label)%>%
  dplyr::select(Sample,TISSUE_PHENOTYPE)%>%
  dplyr::rename("Cell_type"=TISSUE_PHENOTYPE)

distmat <- cophenetic(drop.tip(tree.corrected.ultra,"Ancestral"))

amova_res<-amova_test(distmat = distmat,
                      cell_key = cellkey,
                      iterations = 30000,
                      plottitle = paste0(sample_ID,": Phylogenetic clustering by cell source:\ncorrected ultrametric tree"),
                      file = if(resave_plots) paste0(plots_dir,sample_ID,"_AMOVA_corrected_tree.pdf") else NULL)
amova_res

```

```{r mutlist1, eval=TRUE}
})
```

### Option 2: Shared mutations + likely clonal mutations + 15 x complete mutation sets
Create a csv file of more selected mutations from both mice.
These includes:
1) All shared mutations
2) Private mutations identified as most likely to be clonal (those with a VAF>0.45 and with depth > 15X)
3) All private mutations from a selected subset of samples (15 per mouse)

```{r mutlist2,eval=FALSE}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = my_working_dir,echo = TRUE)

reselect_tips=F

if(!reselect_tips) {
  selected_colony_df<-readr::read_csv("selected_tips.csv")
  
} else {

  
  #Write dataframe of the selected colonies for resequencing
selected_colony_df<-dplyr::bind_rows(all.muts)%>%
  filter(selected_tip)%>%
  dplyr::select(sample_ID,node)%>%
  filter(!duplicated(.))%>%
  arrange(sample_ID,node)

selected_colony_df$colony_ID<-sapply(1:nrow(selected_colony_df),function(i) {all.trees[[selected_colony_df$sample_ID[i]]]$tip.label[selected_colony_df$node[i]]})

readr::write_csv(x = selected_colony_df,file="selected_tips.csv")
}

all.muts<-lapply(sample_IDs, function(this_sample_ID) {
  load(paste0(my_working_dir,"annotated_muts/annotated_mut_set_",this_sample_ID,"_postMS_reduced_a_j_vaf_post_mix_post_dup"))
  details<-filtered_muts$COMB_mats.tree.build$mat
  tree<-all.trees[[this_sample_ID]]
  COMB_mats=filtered_muts$COMB_mats.tree.build
  COMB_mats$NR[COMB_mats$NR == 0] <- 1
  
  details<-details%>%mutate(sample_ID=this_sample_ID,.before=1)
  
  #Add this info to the details matrix (this is the variant and depth counts within samples that should be positive)
  details$NV=sapply(1:nrow(details),function(i) {
    Samples=getTips(tree = tree,node = details$node[i])
    return(sum(COMB_mats$NV[details$mut_ref[i],Samples]))
  })
  details$NR=sapply(1:nrow(details),function(i) {
    Samples=getTips(tree = tree,node = details$node[i])
    return(sum(COMB_mats$NR[details$mut_ref[i],Samples]))
  })
  
  #Also chose 15 samples for which to do ALL mutations - to get a sense of the true specificity
  n_colonies_per_mouse=15
  set.seed(41)
  selected_tips<-selected_colony_df%>%filter(sample_ID==this_sample_ID)%>%pull(node)
  
  details$shared<-ifelse(details$node%in%1:length(tree$tip.label),F,T)
  details$selected_tip<-ifelse(details$node%in%selected_tips,T,F)

  return(details)
})
```

## Check the bait set for which mutations are covered in each tree

Read in the baitset probe info from the TWIST design summary files
Find overlaps between the probes and the mutations and use these to create a new field: 'covered_final'.
Plot the trees to show the covered mutations

```{r baitset_check}
#----FINAL CHECK FOR WHICH MUTATIONS ARE COVERED (after resubmitting final designs)------------------------------

baitset_file=paste0(my_working_dir,"baitset_design/Sanger_Mouse_phylo_REDUCED_v2_TE-99621817_mm10/merged_probe_file_shareable_Sanger_Mouse_phylo_REDUCED_v2_TE-99621817_mm10_low.bed")
cat_bed=read.delim(baitset_file,header = F,col.names = c("Chr","Start","End","Probe_ID"))
cat_bed$Chr<-gsub("chr","",cat_bed$Chr)
covered_regions_GR<-GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(cat_bed,seqnames.field = "Chr",start.field = "Start",end.field = "End")

all.muts<-lapply(all.muts,function(details) {
  details$covered_final=0
  
  #Intersect each details coordinates with the final covered regions
  details_GR<-GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(details,seqnames.field = "Chrom",start.field="Pos",end.field = "Pos")
  overlaps<-GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(covered_regions_GR,details_GR)
  details$covered_final[overlaps@to] <- 1 #Record that each mutation at that coordinate is covered by the final baitset
  return(details)
})

#Write bed file of the covered indels and SNVs
dplyr::bind_rows(all.muts)%>%
  filter(covered_final==1 & Mut_type=="SNV")%>%
  dplyr::select(Chrom,Pos,Ref,Alt)%>%
  arrange(Chrom,Pos)%>%
  readr::write_delim(file="baitset_SNVs.bed",delim = "\t",col_names = F)

dplyr::bind_rows(all.muts)%>%
  filter(covered_final==1 & Mut_type=="INDEL")%>%
  dplyr::select(Chrom,Pos,Ref,Alt)%>%
  arrange(Chrom,Pos)%>%
  readr::write_delim(file="baitset_INDELs.bed",delim = "\t",col_names = F)

#Plot the complete trees
# Can see the mutations from the 15selected tips
temp=Map(details=all.muts,tree=all.trees,SampleID=names(all.trees),function(details,tree,SampleID){
  details$is.in.baitset <- details$covered_final == 1
  #tree=squash_tree(tree,cut_off=15)
  tree=plot_tree(tree, cex.label = 0,title = paste0(SampleID,": covered mutations (complete tree)"))
  add_annotation(tree=tree,
                 details=details,
                 list(),
                 annot_function=function(tree,details,matrices,node) {
                   add_binary_proportion(tree,details,matrices,node,bfield = "is.in.baitset",lwd = 1.5)
                 }
  )
})

temp=Map(details=all.muts,tree=all.trees,SampleID=names(all.trees),function(details,tree,SampleID){
  details$is.in.baitset <- details$covered_final == 1
  tree=squash_tree(tree,cut_off=15)
  tree=plot_tree(tree, cex.label = 0,title = paste0(SampleID,": covered mutations (cut tree)"))
  add_annotation(tree=tree,
                 details=details,
                 list(),
                 annot_function=function(tree,details,matrices,node) {
                   add_binary_proportion(tree,details,matrices,node,bfield = "is.in.baitset",lwd = 1.5)
                 }
  )
})
```
